body.cap: WiseJet’s exclusive booth featured cutting-edge wireless data and power transmission technology at CES 2025. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Korean company WiseJet (CEO Chul Soon Park) is making waves at CES 2025 with its ambitious vision of eliminating cables from all electronic devices and robots. By presenting its advanced wireless data and power transmission technology, WiseJet set new standards for innovation in the robotics industry.
"WiseJet Technology Becomes an Essential Solution for Global Robotics Companies"

CES 2025, held in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10, highlighted various robotics innovations, including combat, industrial, and household robots. WiseJet gained significant attention by showcasing its wireless solutions for robotic joints, drawing keen interest from leading global robotics firms.

WiseJet’s booth attracted over 110 companies, with approximately 50 major robotics, automotive, and consumer electronics companies initiating follow-up meetings. A company representative stated, "The high interest in WiseJet’s technology at CES has opened doors for global collaborations."

body.cap: Various WiseJet chip-based modules featured wireless data and power transmission technology. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: "Wireless Data and Power Transmission: A Revolutionary Proposal for Robot Design"

WiseJet introduced a chip module capable of wirelessly transmitting data and power simultaneously, which is crucial for robotic joints. The system can transfer power wirelessly over distances of 1-10mm, eliminating the wear and speed limitations of traditional mechanical power supply methods. This breakthrough enables 360-degree rotation and unrestricted movement for robotic components.

Unlike traditional data-only transmission solutions, WiseJet’s technology integrates power transmission, providing enhanced flexibility and durability, fundamentally reshaping robot design and operation.
"WiseJet’s Bold Vision for a Cable-Free Future Gains Attention"
At CES 2025, WiseJet’s chip module-based wireless data and power supply method received high praise for simplifying complex cable designs while ensuring efficient power delivery.

Global robotics companies see WiseJet’s technology as a crucial component for robotic joint design, offering enhanced reliability and design flexibility. CEO Chul Soon Park stated, "CES has confirmed that our technology can play a vital role in the global robotics industry. We also anticipate expansion opportunities in autonomous vehicles, medical devices, and other industries."

body.cap: WiseJet demonstrated its wireless power transmission technology using a chip-based modular monitor (left), repeatedly attaching and detaching it to showcase real-time operation. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Additionally, WiseJet unveiled its ‘Wireless CMOS Solution,’ utilizing 60GHz high-speed wireless communication technology to pioneer new horizons in ultra-high-speed, high-definition data transmission. Notably, its ‘XR-JET’ chip, capable of transmitting 8K/60Hz ultra-high-definition video over 10 meters with latency under 1 ms, garnered attention from the global TV and consumer electronics industry.
AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
